mentions.name: Bookmarker
mentions.description: Bookmarker is a bookmarking app with a conversational assistant UX that explores your saved library with you. It offers tag discovery, color browsing, weekly digests, and smart collections that auto-curate as you save. Semantic search runs hybrid, combining keyword matching with pgvector cosine similarity on 768-dimension embeddings, and responses are streamed.
mentions.problem: The first version had a dead-end search box with six starter prompts (one referencing a tool that didn't exist), no follow-ups, and no guided flows, so users got an answer and had to invent the next question from scratch.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Designing a conversational UX for Bookmarker.

I was stuck on this conversation problem. First version had a dead-end search box: six starter prompts, one referencing a tool that didn't exist. No follow-ups. No guided flows. Users got an answer and had to invent the next question from scratch.

Now the assistant explores your library with you. Tag discovery, color browsing, weekly digests, smart collections that auto-curate as you save.
